To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
C-S lyase enzymes in plants are developmentally regulated and differentially inhibited.

C-S lyase (EC 4.4.1.1) activities are present in the leaves of crucifers (Brassica and Arabidopsis) and non-cruciferous species (barley, Nicotiana and Allium), and are involved in primary (amino acids) and secondary (glucosinolates) metabolism.

C-S lyases are involved in the biosynthesis and metabolism of sulphur compounds, and that at least two distinct C-S lyase classes are present in plants, with one class being specific for aromatic compounds, and the other for both aliphatic- and aromatic-containing compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a number of C-S lyases and their role in glucosinolates biosynthesis in oilseed rape.
the identification of C-S lyases involved in primary and glucosinolate metabolism, and the characterization and purification of the major C-S lyases from rape leaves.
the biochemical characterization of a number of C-S lyases from plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C-S lyase enzymes in plants may have multiple physiological roles.
the C-S lyase enzyme system in higher plants is a complex system, with several distinct activities present.
C-S lyases are present in both glucosinolate and non-glucinolate-containing species, but that the highest activities are in glucosinolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C-S lyase enzymes in plants are capable of cleaving an array of sulphur-containing conjugates, and may have a role in sulphur metabolism in addition to their involvement in glucosinolates.
there are at least three classes (and probably more) of C-S lyases, and that these enzymes are involved in a variety of sulphate-containing metabolites in plant cells.
the C-S lyase enzymes are a heterogeneous group, which may be involved in the degradation of a range of compounds in plant tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

C-S lyase enzymes are present in a wide variety of species, but that the highest activities are present in crucifers, and that the enzymes are developmentally regulated and have distinct biochemical characteristics.
C-S lyases are widespread in plants.
C-S lyase in glucosinolates-containing species are involved in the degradation of the aromatic intermediates of glucosinolate synthesis.
